data.generation: Euler-Maruyama at dt_fine = 0.01 for the Day 8 ground-truth jump-diffusion (see ground_truth_sde). Within each fine step a jump occurs with probability lambda(x) * dt_fine and size drawn from N(mu_J, sigma_J^2). Observations every 0.05 on [0, 10] (201 points per trajectory).

distillation.lambda_fit: lambda is fitted directly (not log lambda) so that negativity of the symbolic lambda on the grid is visible as a domain failure; a log-lambda degree-2 fit is reported as a diagnostic only, never selected.
distillation.library_variables: All libraries are polynomials in the single state x only (the truth is time-homogeneous and one-dimensional). Drift candidates include both free libraries and no-intercept libraries (Day 7 structural-constraint reflection: a no-intercept library is the structural constraint for a drift that vanishes at the origin).
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed states of each split (trajectory-disjoint train/validation/test), teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.form: dX = f(X) dt + g dW + J dN(lambda(X)), where N is a Poisson process with state-dependent intensity lambda(X) and J ~ N(mu_J, sigma_J^2) independent of W and N. This is the paper's jump form dz = f dt + w dN (state-dependent intensity lambda(z), jump function w) with the continuous part extended by a Brownian diffusion term (declared deviation: the paper's continuous part is a deterministic ODE, so a diffusion term is added to make diffusion/jump disentangling testable in observed increments).
ground_truth_sde.lambda: lambda(x) = 0.25 + 0.08 * x^2 (state-dependent intensity, polynomial of degree 2, bounded below by 0.25).

H2_diffusion_distillation.note: Headline is the g NRMSE; the Sigma clause is the identified-object clause (Sigma = g^2 in 1D). Both must hold.

H2j_jump_distillation.note: mu_J and sigma_J are compared as train-query means of the teacher nets versus the symbolic (degree 0/1) fits evaluated at the same states; both must hold together with the lambda clause.

H3_truth_recovery.note: Field-level clauses only; the coefficient clause H3c is separate (Day 1 lesson).

H3c_linear_coefficient.note: Pre-frozen diagnostic fit, NOT the selected model: an origin-pinned degree-2 drift fit at threshold 0.05 (mean-0 standardization, no constant term, so the expanded original-coordinate polynomial genuinely vanishes at x = 0), fitted on train queries and evaluated on test queries. The degree-3 library VIF (maximum selectable degree, intercept column excluded) is 1.46-3.72, i.e. low, so the gate does not forbid a coefficient verdict; the frozen-degree diagnostic is kept as the verdict vehicle to satisfy the Day 7 lesson. Compared quantity: the expanded linear coefficient of f (truth -0.60). Lambda coefficients from a fixed degree-2 fit are tabulated without a verdict.

H4_simulation.domain_excursion_definition: fraction of simulated trajectories whose |X| ever exceeds 8.0 at any simulated step; a domain-validity measure separate from failure (Day 4 reflection).
H4_simulation.note: Paired RMSE is the per-step absolute distance between symbolic and teacher simulated states, median over test trajectories and steps; the threshold is loose (1.0) because jump-timing differences dominate it, so it is NOT the main simulation clause -- failure, excursion and lambda-clip rates carry the verdict. Failure is non-finite state or |X| > 30. Symbolic lambda is clipped at 0 in simulation and sigma_J at 0.01; clipped-step fractions are counted as domain measures.

large_increment_clause.note: MAIN clause is the pair of absolute levels, pre-decided (Day 7 reflection): the simulated large-increment rate of the symbolic model must be within 0.01 of the observed test-transition large-increment rate, and the jump teacher's simulated rate must also be within 0.01 of it, while the diffusion-only teacher's simulated rate must miss by more than 0.01. Large increment = |Delta X| > 0.5 over one dt_obs step (diffusion-only step sd is 0.35*sqrt(0.05) = 0.078, so 0.5 is ~6.4 diffusion sigmas; observed large increments are jump-dominated).

nll_clause.note: Test-transition predictive NLL per transition: jump teacher (2-component Gaussian mixture density) versus diffusion-only teacher (Gaussian density). Clause: NLL(diffusion-only) - NLL(jump) > 0.02 nats and > 2 x paired SE of per-transition NLL differences. Absolute NLL levels for both teachers are reported alongside (Day 7 reflection: absolute levels, not only a difference).

H6_discretization_bias_em_coarsening.coarsening: Jump-mixture EM teacher retrained on observations subsampled to Delta t = 0.5 (every 10th observation) vs jump-mixture EM teacher trained on the same number of transitions subsampled from Delta t = 0.05 data (transition-count-matched, Day 6 lesson). Coarse mixture uses jump probability 1 - exp(-lambda * dt) and a single-jump Gaussian component (multiple jumps within dt = 0.5 have probability ~1% at lambda ~ 0.3 and are neglected; declared approximation).
H6_discretization_bias_em_coarsening.note: Day 1 reflection adapted to jump-diffusions, with Day 6/7 regime lessons: the hypothesis is regime-split by |x| (small |x| < 0.5 vs large |x| > 1.5), and per-transition SNR is quantified (drift signal |f| dt against diffusion sd g sqrt(dt), by regime) alongside transition-count matching. Drift and diffusion coarse-vs-fine comparisons are interpreted separately (Day 7: diffusion estimation is dominated by sample size, not step size). A jump-contamination diagnostic is reported separately: the diffusion-only teacher's g versus truth (jumps absorbed into g) and a jump-screened two-stage g estimate (|Delta| > 0.4 screened out) versus truth.

H7_downstream_one_step.note: |MSE_symbolic - MSE_teacher| for one-step-ahead mean predictions on test transitions, where the predicted mean is x + f dt + mu_J * lambda * dt (expected increment including jumps) and the target is the realized next state. Paired SE reported; if paired SE >= 0.001 (half the threshold) the clause is reported as 'not statistically established' even if the point estimate passes (Day 4 reflection).

paper.experiment: Sections 3-4: Neural Jump SDEs extend Neural ODEs with a stochastic jump term dz = f(z) dt + w(z) dN(t), where events occur with state-dependent conditional intensity lambda(z); gradients through discontinuities via a lifted adjoint. Demonstrated on synthetic and real marked point-process data (classical point processes such as Hawkes, Stack Overflow awards, medical records, earthquake monitoring) for prediction of future events.
paper.title: Neural Jump Stochastic Differential Equations

reflections_applied.day1_collinearity_gate_at_max_degree: VIF is computed on train queries for the degree-3 library (the maximum degree the selection procedure can choose), with the constant column excluded (its VIF is meaningless). The resulting VIFs are 1.46-3.72 (low), so the gate passes; H3c still uses a pre-frozen origin-pinned degree-2 diagnostic fit as the verdict vehicle (Day 7 lesson).
reflections_applied.day1_discretization_bias: H6 is the adapted discretization-bias diagnostic: jump-mixture EM at Delta t = 0.5 vs transition-count-matched Delta t = 0.05, regime-split by |x|, with per-transition SNR quantified by regime and drift/diffusion interpreted separately. A jump-contamination diagnostic for g (diffusion-only teacher vs jump-screened two-stage estimate) is the Day 1 linear/nonlinear g-comparison analogue: jumps contaminate g in the unscreened estimator.
reflections_applied.day2_off_manifold: Off-manifold diagnostic is standard: a fixed grid x in [-4, 4] (81 points, extending well beyond the data range) for f, g and lambda, reported on field / off-manifold axes separately and used for reporting only, never for selection (Day 5). Grid points outside the data range carry no strong extrapolation claim (Day 3).
reflections_applied.day4_domain_validity: H4 carries domain clauses separate from failure: |X| excursion (> 8) and symbolic lambda clip rate (negative lambda clipped at 0 in simulation), the jump-specific domain measure.
reflections_applied.day4_downstream_paired_se: H5 NLL clause and H7 report paired SEs with pre-frozen indeterminate rules.
reflections_applied.day5_distribution_vs_field: No distribution-matching teacher is used (all teachers are transition-likelihood mixture EM), so no distribution-loss verdict can be confused with a field verdict; teacher-vs-truth and symbolic-vs-teacher errors are tabulated side by side, and H5 reports absolute NLL levels for both teachers.
reflections_applied.day5_multiple_initial_conditions: Every trajectory has its own Normal(0, 1) initial state (no single initial condition).
reflections_applied.day5_off_manifold_denominator: Grid NRMSE values above 1 are reported with absolute RMS errors alongside.
reflections_applied.day6_diffusion_input_design: Diffusion and jump parameters are fitted and verified separately from drift (g, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J each have their own library and verdict); a trajectory-constant input failure mode of the Day 6 type cannot arise here because all libraries take only the current state x.
reflections_applied.day7_absolute_levels_for_shift: H5's main clause is pre-decided as absolute levels (simulated vs observed large-increment rates for each model), not only a degradation/difference; the NLL clause additionally reports absolute NLL levels for both teachers.
reflections_applied.day7_rare_domain_events: Lambda negativity is a potentially rare on-manifold event (lambda is bounded below by 0.25 in truth), so it is tested on the wide off-manifold grid (81 points to |x| = 4) rather than by counting rare on-manifold occurrences, and the symbolic clip rate in simulation is counted over all simulated steps.
reflections_applied.day7_structural_library: Drift candidates include origin-pinned libraries, implemented as mean-0 standardization with no constant term (an implementation note: a no-intercept library in standardized coordinates pins the fit at the train mean, not at the origin -- the first implementation had exactly this bug, visible as a 0.34 diagnostic NRMSE, and was corrected before the final run). Validation selected the free library, because the teacher itself has f(0) = -0.072, not 0; the origin diagnostic is reported alongside.

simulation.jump_pairing: shared Brownian increments, shared uniform jump draws and shared jump-size normals across models; each model decides jumps from its own lambda(x) (U < 1 - exp(-lambda dt))

teacher.architecture: Jump teacher: five small MLPs on standardized x only (truth is time-homogeneous): f net [32, 32] tanh; g net [16] tanh, output softplus + 0.01; log-lambda net [16] tanh, lambda = softplus(raw) + 0.01; mu_J net [16] tanh; log-sigma_J net [16] tanh, sigma_J = softplus(raw) + 0.05. Diffusion-only teacher: f net [32, 32] tanh and g net [16] tanh, Gaussian EM NLL. All teachers trained by Adam on train transitions only.
teacher.deviation_from_paper: Three declared cuts. (1) Latent point-process pipeline replaced by an identifiable observable 1D jump-diffusion: the paper's latent trajectory, adjoint training through event times, and marked point-process benchmarks (Hawkes, Stack Overflow, MIMIC, earthquakes) are not treated; the teacher is reconstructed in identifiable coordinates as an observable jump-diffusion whose jump part follows the paper's form (state-dependent intensity lambda(z), jump function w). (2) Continuous part extended with a Brownian diffusion term: the paper's continuous dynamics are a deterministic ODE plus jumps, so a diffusion term is added to make diffusion/jump disentangling testable in observed increments; results therefore do not reproduce the paper's model class exactly. (3) Training is by a two-component Gaussian-mixture transition likelihood (no-jump vs one-jump component, jump probability 1 - exp(-lambda dt)) rather than the paper's adjoint point-process likelihood; this is the series' standard estimator and is declared as a method substitution.

em_coarse.transitions: train trajectories subsampled to every 10th observation (480 x 20 = 9600 transitions)

em_fine_sub.transitions: 9600 transitions subsampled at random (seed-fixed) from train Delta t = 0.05 transitions, matching the coarsened count

teacher.estimator: jump-mixture EM (two-component Gaussian transition likelihood, variable dt not needed: regular grid)

estimators_compared.jump_coarse: jump-mixture EM on subsampled Delta t = 0.5 train transitions
estimators_compared.jump_diffusion_only: Gaussian EM (no jump component) on full regular train transitions -- the paper-axis baseline
estimators_compared.jump_fine_sub: jump-mixture EM on transition-count-matched Delta t = 0.05 train transitions
estimators_compared.jump_main: jump-mixture EM on full regular train transitions (dt = 0.05) -- the distilled teacher
